title: Extension of divided powers along a flat ring map
statement: Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $f:A\to B$ a unital ring map that is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with an ordinary divided-power structure $\gamma$ [def-sfb-ordinary-divided-power-structure]. Write $IB$ for the ideal of $B$ generated by $f(I)$. There is a unique ordinary divided-power structure $\bar\gamma$ on $IB$ for which $\bar\gamma_n(f(x))=f(\gamma_n(x))$ for $x\in I$ and $n\geq1$.

source.place: Tag 07H1 (lemma-gamma-extends), uniqueness and existence under condition (3), flatness.

proof.text: For $z=\sum_i b_i f(x_i)\in IB$ with $x_i\in I$, use the expression $P_n(x;b)$ of [lem-sfb-pd-linear-substitution]. Any extension must have this value: induction on the number of summands using the addition axiom expands its $n$th operation into the sum over $e_1+\cdots+e_r=n$, and the scalar axiom replaces each factor by $b_i^{e_i}f(\gamma_{e_i}(x_i))$. Thus at most one extension exists. For $n>0$ every summand belongs to $IB$, since some $e_i>0$ and $\gamma_{e_i}(x_i)\in I$.

source.place: Tag 07H1, uniqueness paragraph and flat-case displayed formula.

proof.text: To show that the formula is independent of the presentation, let $\sum_i b_if(x_i)=\sum_k b'_kf(x'_k)$. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $B$ is a flat $A$-module via $f$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-equational-criterion] to the single relation with coefficient tuple $(x_i,-x'_k)$ and module tuple $(b_i,b'_k)$. It gives $c_j\in B$, $a_{ij},a'_{kj}\in A$ with $b_i=\sum_jf(a_{ij})c_j$, $b'_k=\sum_jf(a'_{kj})c_j$ and $\sum_i x_i a_{ij}=\sum_k x'_k a'_{kj}=:y_j$ in $A$. The $y_j$ lie in $I$. Apply [lem-sfb-pd-linear-substitution] separately to the two tuples: both expressions become $P_n(y;c)$. Thus define $\bar\gamma_n(z)=P_n(x;b)$ for any presentation of $z$, for $n>0$, and put $\bar\gamma_0(z)=1$.

source.place: Tag 07H1, flat-case common refinement and footnote using Tag 00HK (algebra.tex, lemma-flat-eq).

proof.text: The degree-one formula is $\bar\gamma_1(\sum_i b_if(x_i))=\sum_i b_if(x_i)$. Replacing all $b_i$ by $cb_i$ multiplies every summand of degree $n$ by $c^n$, proving $\bar\gamma_n(cz)=c^n\bar\gamma_n(z)$. For presentations of $z$ and $w$, concatenate their tuples. Partitioning the degree-$n$ multiindices according to the total degree $a$ in the first block and $n-a$ in the second gives exactly $\bar\gamma_n(z+w)=\sum_{a=0}^n\bar\gamma_a(z)\bar\gamma_{n-a}(w)$. These arguments use only the now well-defined finite formula. In particular $\bar\gamma_n(0)=0$ for $n>0$, by taking the empty presentation.

source.place: Tag 07H1, final paragraph: conditions (1),(3),(4) by construction.

proof.text: For the one-term presentation $f(x)=1\cdot f(x)$ the formula gives $\bar\gamma_n(f(x))=f(\gamma_n(x))$ for every $x\in I$ and $n\geq0$. On the generating set $f(I)$, the product identity follows by applying $f$ to the product identity for $\gamma$. Also $\gamma_m(x)\in I$, so $\bar\gamma_n(\bar\gamma_m(f(x)))=f(\gamma_n(\gamma_m(x)))$; apply $f$ to the iteration identity for $\gamma$. Thus the two remaining axioms hold on $f(I)$. This set generates $IB$ by its definition. The maps land in $IB$ by step 1 and satisfy the three global axioms by step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-pd-generator-criterion] to obtain all divided-power axioms on $IB$. Together with the compatibility just proved and uniqueness in step 1 this proves the item.

source.place: Tag 07H1, last two sentences, invoking Tag 07GP (lemma-check-on-generators).
